newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India prices higher in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India prices higher in thin trade.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) continued to firm on Tuesday, but traders said activity was thin.
"There's some nibbly buying but no supply. Once again we've been caught without enough supply," one trader said.
The Cazenove Indian GDR Index rose 1.13 points to 66.82 on Tuesday after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index added 26.56 points to 2,985.21.
The GDR premium over stocks on the local market was also higher at 15.35 percent.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index rose 2.75 percent to 61.52 by 1640 GMT, with the premium over the local market at 20.85 percent.
The gains were across the board.
Bajaj Autos, which has already surged over 20 percent in the past few days, was up another $2.08 at $30.75.
The latest gains come on the back of the stronger local market which on Tuesday was given a fresh boost by the government's move to drop a non-voting share proposal.
Also, speculation that the government would remove or change the minimum alternate tax (MAT) continued to give support to the market.
